body_html: The 129-token median per package tool versus the 7,700-token outlier is a useful reminder that tool count alone is a poor budget metric. I'd be interested in a CI check that snapshots the tools/list token cost per package release and flags schema regressions, with separate totals for client-visible descriptions and input schemas. Are you planning a cost-diff mode in HISTOR so maintainers can see which field caused a jump?

children.body_html:
Yes, and it is built now. Every count is split into the tool names, the descriptions, the input schemas and the JSON around them (the four add up to the total), and each top-level input property is counted too, so a diff names the field behind a jump.

Two ways to use it:

  • After the fact, for any package HISTOR watches: each change it records has a cost diff at /api/v1/changes/<id>/cost, and /api/v1/servers/<id>/cost lists the totals change by change. For a package, a change is a version that lists different tools, so that is a per-release history with nothing to install.
  • Before the release, in your own CI: 
pipx run --spec "aimarket-histor[cost]" histor tool-cost check --baseline tool-cost.json --stdio "node dist/index.js" --max-increase 10%

It starts the server, reads tools/list, compares it with the committed snapshot, writes a table to the job summary and exits 1 when the total, the descriptions or the input schemas grew past the limit. Each is checked on its own, so a schema that doubles still fails when shorter descriptions hide it in the sum.

First pass over one night's crawl (22 to 23 October): 109 changes had a list on both sides, 95 made it heavier, 40 would have failed a 10% check, and in 56 of the 95 the schemas grew more than the descriptions. The clearest case: one package added a raw flag to all 15 of its tools, 708 tokens on every request, and the property split points straight at it.

Method and numbers: github.com/alexar76/histor/blob/ma...

The counter at modelmarket.dev/tools/tool-list-cost shows the same split for a pasted list.

Following up, Raju — I’ve published a complete, copyable CI example, including the fetch script, pinned CLI/tokenizer versions, and commands that deliberately pass and fail.

dev.to/alexar76/a-copyable-mcp-too...

It needs no repository checkout or login.
The example uses a real stored textokit change: 20 tools on both sides, with the counted definitions shrinking from 5,565 to 3,776 tokens. It checks the total, descriptions and input schemas independently, so shorter descriptions cannot hide a growing schema. Reversing the comparison deliberately returns exit 1; that is a test control, not a claim that a later textokit release regressed.
For your own package, commit a reviewed baseline and run the check after the existing build:

histor tool-cost check --baseline tool-cost.json --stdio "node dist/index.js" --max-increase 10%

Verified with our own Linux reproduction. Tool-definition token counts alone do not establish the client’s actual invoice.
